text:
New Jersey traded for Connor Hellebuyck in late October because its biggest weakness was obvious, and so far the move has been as much a story as a fix. On Tuesday the Devils sat him in Winnipeg for his first game against his old team. The Jets won 4-2, with two goals from Dawson Mercer and 19 saves from Nico Daws, two of the players New Jersey sent the other way. That snapped a five-game winning streak.

One loss doesn't change much. The Devils are 13-6-0 and get 58% of the expected goals (the quality of chances), the best share in this group of teams, and they allow fewer chances per hour than anyone here. Jack Hughes, Jesper Bratt and Arseny Gritsyuk have outscored teams 12-3 at five on five. Nico Hischier just reached 500 career points, and his line with Timo Meier and Luke Evangelista is nearly as dominant. Luke Hughes and Brett Pesce are plus ten together.

The flaw has been the crease: Devils goalies have allowed almost six more goals than expected. That's exactly the hole Hellebuyck was brought in to fill, and if he plays like the Hellebuyck of the last few seasons, a team at 93% to make the playoffs in our simulations becomes a real threat in the East.

They also stay out of the box, drawing more than a penalty a game more than they take. What to watch: Hellebuyck's save percentage over the next month. Everything else is already in place.
headline: The Devils got their goalie. Now use him.
